claims_about_writeup.why: This is simply a pointer to the write-up file, which does exist and contains the method description described in the message; no specific content claim is made beyond its existence/location.

message_source_quote: The white-bear steering paper (Raman 2026) works on exactly this setup (0.83) but extracts its direction from WorkspaceBench's `directed_modulation` bench family — a dependency the task's "new method, not a reproduction" rule pushes against.
writeup_source_quote: The starting point is the white-bear steering result of Raman et al. (2026), who show that a think/don't-think stance direction added at mid depth makes implied concepts readable through the plain J-lens on this exact setup.

differences.what: Raman et al.'s reported fit pass@10 score for their original method on this setup
differences.message_quote: The white-bear steering paper (Raman 2026) works on exactly this setup (0.83)

differences.what: Number and identity of failed alternative contrasts tested (write-up lists three; message lists four, including a 'concept-free think/don't-think' variant, with specific per-contrast numbers)
differences.message_quote: concept-free think/don't-think ("what this brings to mind") | ~0.03 (harms)
differences.writeup_quote: I tried three contrasts that drop it — an "identify-the-implied-category" framing, a few-shot function-vector prompt, and a dual-task "keep something in mind while copying" stance — and all three leave pass@10 at or below baseline.

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. (2026)'s white-bear steering as the explicit source and starting point, describe the method as building on/overlapping with it (think/don't-think stance direction at mid-depth read through the plain J-lens), and claim the same novelty: replacing the bench-derived directed_modulation contrast with a small, self-authored, concept-disjoint stance bank to remove the benchmark dependency while keeping the suppression-pole mechanism load-bearing. The message adds a couple of extra numeric/mechanism details (Raman's own fit score of 0.83, and one additional failed-contrast ablation with per-row numbers) not present in the write-up, but these are numeric/mechanism details rather than changes to the source's identity, the overlap claim, or the novelty claim, so overall treatment is equivalent.
